circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It was the second Middle Eastern grand prix location to join the calendar, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit is a street-based racing venue situated around a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb. The track hosts the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix along with supporting motorsport events, and maintains the highest FIA safety certification for circuits.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally opened as Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix continuously throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a reconstruction and renaming during the 1990s, the venue returned to hosting the Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, stretching 6. 003 km to rank as the fourth-longest venue on the F1 calendar. The circuit hosted its first Formula One race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 kilometers and hosted the inaugural Middle Eastern Formula One Grand Prix that year. Beyond F1, the venue accommodates various racing series including GP2, 24-hour endurance competitions, and previously the Australian V8 Supercars, holding a Grade 1 FIA license with multiple track configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km circuit features a balanced combination of high-speed straights and diverse corner configurations that challenge drivers across multiple disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Belgian circuit in Francorchamps spans 7. 004 kilometres and has hosted Formula One's Belgian Grand Prix since 1925, participating in the sport's inaugural season in 1950. The venue has maintained an unbroken presence on the F1 calendar from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361 km track serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its current status as a premier single-seater venue, the circuit has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships and North American racing programs.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in China's Jiading district served as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 until 2019, with the race returning to the venue from 2024 onward. Beyond hosting this flagship Formula One event, the track has expanded its motorsport calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, England, Silverstone Circuit hosted the inaugural 1948 British Grand Prix and later staged the first-ever World Championship race in 1950. After alternating with two other venues for three decades, the British Grand Prix has been permanently based at Silverstone since 1987, which also features in the MotoGP calendar.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986, just eight months after construction began. Located in Mogyoród outside the capital, this 4. 381 km circuit was built as an alternative to a proposed Monaco-style street course, and the inaugural race commemorated Hungarian motorcycle racing pioneer János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. The track earned its "Temple of Speed" nickname through its extended straights and rapid cornering sections, and has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, making it one of only four circuits that have remained on the Formula One calendar from the championship's inception, with a single interruption in 1980 for renovations.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track hosts major international racing events, most notably Formula One and Super Formula championships, with a spectator capacity of 155,000.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course situated in Paradise, Nevada that navigates through the famous entertainment district of Las Vegas. The layout weaves past iconic casino and hotel properties including Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, as well as the MSG Sphere venue.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: This 4. 3 km circuit in Mexico City is named after two Mexican racing brothers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who both died in racing accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue returned to hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix in 2015 after a 23-year absence, with the race now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021, though the track operates on a different configuration than the circuit used during its previous hosting periods that ended in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for the Miami Grand Prix, the track joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 and has since been adapted for other racing series, including electric vehicles from 2025–26 onwards.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts along Monaco's harbour, though it is popularly known as the Monte Carlo circuit since much of the layout occupies that specific neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, this 4. 259 km circuit hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix after returning to Formula One in 2021, though the partnership concluded in 2026. The track, situated north of Zandvoort close to the North Sea, has operated under its current sponsored name since mid-2025.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is situated near Lusail, north of Doha in Qatar, and features a 5. 419 km layout with a 1. 068 km main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aircraft accident in 1977. The counterclockwise layout hosts prestigious motor racing events and shares its facilities with a kart track dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has served as the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its debut in 2021. The circuit began hosting an electric racing series event starting in 2025 alongside its primary Formula One commitment.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, incorporating the Downtown Core and Kallang areas in its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya near Barcelona spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for all racing disciplines. The venue accommodates 140,700 spectators and maintains FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major international motorsport events including MotoGP and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race. The track has also accommodated various racing series over the years, ranging from NASCAR to IndyCar and sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon represents Thailand in Formula One racing while driving for Williams. The Anglo-Thai driver has established himself as a competitor in the sport's premier championship.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 and achieved 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond his single-seater success, Alonso has distinguished himself in endurance racing by winning the World Endurance Championship, two Le Mans 24-hour races, and the Daytona 24-hour event, making him the sole driver to excel in both Formula One and world sportscar championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes on the Formula One grid, having secured eight race victories since entering the championship in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently racing for Haas in Formula One's premier championship series.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One with the Audi team, bringing his competitive motorsport background to the sport's highest level.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas competes in Formula One for Cadillac and has secured two World Drivers' Championship runner-up finishes during his time with Mercedes. Throughout his 13-season career in the sport, he has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas while competing in European Le Mans Series prototypes for Nielsen Racing. He has made seven Formula One appearances spanning the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver achieved victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri earlier in his career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: A French-Algerian driver competing for Red Bull Racing, Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One competition.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding a shared record of seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. The veteran competitor leads in multiple all-time statistics, including victories, pole positions, and podium appearances throughout his career in the sport.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he has achieved success in endurance motorsport, including victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand-born racing driver, currently races in Formula One for the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine-year career. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while driving for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver who has competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024. Currently, he races in the World Endurance Championship driving for BMW through WRT, while also competing part-time in NASCAR's top series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver racing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has secured 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Haas team.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac, bringing extensive experience from a 15-season career that includes six Grand Prix victories. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull before joining his current team.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories since joining the sport four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo, known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has claimed eight Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, bringing experience from 12 seasons in the sport. He has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his career in the series.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously campaigned in IMSA's LMP2 class.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin. He competes at the highest level of motorsport under his commonly used professional name.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently functioning as a reserve for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. He competed in full-time racing capacities from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a reserve role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing under the Dutch flag and has secured four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across 12 seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 72 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China in Formula One as a reserve driver for Cadillac, making history as the sole Chinese competitor to race in the series. He participated in Formula One competition spanning from 2022 through 2024.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based outfit has competed as Alpine since 2021, serving as Renault's factory team and promoting the French automaker's Alpine sports car brand. Previously known as Renault F1 Team, the squad maintained this works partnership until Renault's withdrawal from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has been involved in Formula One through several different team structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari HP represents the Italian automaker's motorsport arm and stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished squad, participating continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. The team's iconic emblem has earned it the enduring moniker "the Prancing Horse" among racing enthusiasts.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with the outfit making its competitive debut during the 2016 season. Following Guenther Steiner's departure in early 2024, Ayao Komatsu assumed the role of team principal.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering firm became an independent Formula One constructor in 1993 and competed for over three decades, ranking as the fourth-longest-serving team in the sport's history. Before joining F1, the operation achieved notable success in endurance racing, including overall victory at the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours. Acquired by Audi in 2024, the team's operations and infrastructure were repurposed as the foundation for Audi's Formula One entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under the McLaren Mastercard F1 Team banner. The organization operates as part of the McLaren Group, which is fully owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and power unit supplier. The current team, competing from its Brackley headquarters under a German licence, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in 2022, with the squad traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team functions as Red Bull's second constructor within the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024, operating as a second team under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the squad operates as part of Red Bull's dual-team structure within the sport.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and part of the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate. Founded in 2005 under Christian Horner's management, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies as team principal in 2025. Red Bull also owns Racing Bulls as its sister team in the championship.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's previous failed racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team name and operates from a substantial 60-acre facility.
